judgments.note: Clearly an appeal of a municipal DRB approval. The subject is an addition to an existing residential treatment center (a care home), but the decision never says whether the addition adds residential beds or only program, school, child-care and office space; the dispute is about non-residential uses. Housing is therefore unknown, making the case uncertain rather than excluded.
If the addition adds no residential capacity it is like a large addition that adds no unit (no); if it expands the residence it could be new housing (care home). The documents do not say which.
The court takes evidence at evidentiary hearings and schedules a merits hearing on the application 'before this Court', which is de novo review; the words 'de novo' do not appear.
Filing date not given; start is the May 11, 2005 revised usage chart filed in the appeal (on_or_before); end is the June 7, 2005 order with hearings still pending (on_or_after); 27 days at least.
The revised usage chart filed May 11, 2005 is the earliest dated event in the appeal; the docket number is not used to date the filing.
The DRB decision date is not stated.
The DRB granted approval; whether conditions were attached is not stated, so 'approved'.
Kevin Fisher is the appellant; his relationship to the property (likely a neighbor) is not stated, so unknown.

The decided motions concern use classification (community house, principal vs accessory uses), largely rule and fact based, but the merits contentions for the later hearing (which may include conditional-use or major-impact criteria) are not described, so unknown.
The DRB approval is on de novo appeal with the merits undecided; no in-docket authorization stands observed, so unknown.
